test_title: PYST 3: SSC CGL Tier - II (Quant) (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: maths
question: By selling an article for Rs. 2,200, a profit of 10% is earned. If the same article is sold for Rs. 2,600, then what will be the gain percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit of 10% implies Selling Price is 110% of Cost Price.

Given: ₹2,200 represents 110%.

New Selling Price % = (New SP ÷ Old SP) × Old %

New Selling Price % = (2,600 ÷ 2,200) × 110% = (13 ÷ 11) × 110% = 130%.

Gain % = 130% − 100% = 30%.

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹2,200

Profit % = 10%

New Selling Price (SP₂) = ₹2,600

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b90c121b4dae7cd7f7a609d29cb444f7ec562ce939b31dbc408a111e5769b62d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = 2200 × [100 ÷ (100 + 10)]

⇒ CP = 2200 × (100 ÷ 110)

⇒ CP = 20 × 100 = ₹2,000

⇒ New Profit = SP₂ − CP = 2600 − 2000 = ₹600

⇒ Gain Percentage = (600 ÷ 2000) × 100

⇒ Gain Percentage = (6 ÷ 20) × 100 = 0.3 × 100 = 30%

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

Two successive discounts of a% and b% are equivalent to a single discount of [a + b − (ab ÷ 100)]%.

Relationship between CP and MP

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%). This is useful for finding mark-up percentage.
